name: Santo Domingo de Morelos Miahuatec Zapotec / 'Santo Domingo de Morelos Zapotec'
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 4 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Hernández Luna, Mario Ulises & Esther Herrera Zendejas. 2024. A phonological sketch of the Santo Domingo de Morelos variety of Miahuatec Zapotec. Cuadernos de Lingüística de El Colegio de México 11, e311, 1-38. DOI 10.24201/clecm.v11i00.311 (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0). Supporting, same author and variety: Hernández Luna, Mario Ulises. 2021. La palabra fonológica en miahuateco. Cuadernos de Lingüística de El Colegio de México 8, e239, 1-37. DOI 10.24201/clecm.v8i0.239; Hernández Luna 2020 [2021]. catalog_locator: 2024 sketch §5 'Prosodic word, syllable structure, and stress', pp. 25-31; cited passage p. 27 (Table 3), summary sentence p. 31. General rule: Hernández Luna 2021 §3 pp. 16-18 (rule statements pp. 16-17; ex. 9 p. 18).
catalog_quote: Even though zam is a monosyllabic language, there are disyllabic morphologically complex words that reveal an iambic stress pattern. The stressed syllable is always heavy while unstressed syllables are always light (Sicoli 2007; Arellanes 2021, among others). This means that bimoraicity is related to both stress and minimality. The prosodic requirement that the minimal word be a bimoraic foot, even when it is a monosyllable, is because a stressed syllable is bimoraic and a prosodic word must have a stressed syllable. Table 3 shows the words [kàː] ‘to move’ and [níː] ‘foot’ in isolation, and finally the compound [kàníː] ‘to dance’. The compound word is formed by an unbalanced iambic foot, a canonical iamb according to Hayes (1995). ... In sum, the most prominent cue of stress in Santo Domingo de Morelos Zapotec is the duration of the rhyme.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File opened: (38 pp., text, InDesign PDF; title/DOI 10.24201/clecm.v11i00.311 in the running header; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 on p. 1). Section 5 'Prosodic word, syllable structure, and stress' runs pp. 25-31 as stated. The quoted passage is on p. 27, every sentence found verbatim (checked sentence by sentence against extracted text output); the only difference is that the quote silently drops one sentence between sentences 2 and 3 ('This means that bimoraicity is related to both stress and minimality.') without an ellipsis. Surrounding section read: p. 25-26 lexicon mostly monosyllabic, minimal word = bimoraic foot; p. 27 Table 3 [kàː] + [níː] > [kàníː] 'to dance', unbalanced iambic foot; pp. 27-31…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The lexicon is overwhelmingly monosyllabic; each prosodic word has exactly one stressed syllable, which is bimoraic (long vowel, or vowel + moraic fortis/sonorant coda). In the polysyllabic words that exist (compounds, na- stative forms, Spanish loans) stress is iambic: it falls on the final syllable of the base, i.e. the right edge of the prosodic word, with preceding syllables light and unstressed. The same author's 2021 CLECM article (same Santo Domingo de Morelos data) states it directly: 'el acento siempre caerá en la sílaba del borde derecho de la base' (p. 17), with right-to-left directionality shown by recursive compounds [jí.síd.ŋɡùð.ˈlòː] 'pestaña'. Acoustic correlate is rhyme duration (stressed rhyme ~2x unstressed), not vowel duration, intensity or F0 (F0 = tone). The language is tonal (H, L, falling, rising) with stress alongside tone.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not described. Beam de Azcona 2016 (San Bartolomé Loxicha Miahuatec slides) raises '¿acento secundario?' for first roots of compounds that retain their tone, without deciding.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated for the position. Bimoraicity is obligatory and culminative (max one bimoraic syllable per word; Hernández Luna 2021 p. 16). Enclitics fall outside the prosodic word (Beam de Azcona 2016: 'los clíticos son extramétricos'; Beam & Cruz Santiago 2022 §2.1). Loans: [mer.kaːð] 'mercado', [ku.tʃiː] 'caballo' with final lengthening (Hernández Luna 2020: 159).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: prosodic word = base (root plus any preceding prefix/compound member), enclitics excluded; statements are based on elicited isolation forms and compounds (109 words x 3 repetitions, two speakers of Santo Domingo de Morelos, Hernández Luna 2021 §3.1; three speakers, fieldwork 2008-2019, for the 2024 sketch). Unstressed (pretonic) syllables lose contrastive tone, glottalization and coda contrasts.
new_statements.identity_note: The deciding sources describe the Santo Domingo de Morelos variety (Pochutla district). The authors label it 'Miahuatec Zapotec (ISO zam)', but Glottolog 5.1 files Hernández Luna's Santo Domingo de Morelos work under loxi1235 (ztp Loxicha Zapotec), and Beam de Azcona & Cruz Santiago 2022 (§2) state that Santo Domingo de Morelos 'pertenece a la misma zona dialectal de San Agustín Loxicha' (the ztp reference town), treating SAL/SDM and San Bartolomé Loxicha (zam) as one language, 'miahuateco'. So the statement is first-hand for a ztp town but is framed by its authors as Miahuatec; the group-level rule (final stress of the lexical word, clitics extrametrical) is independently stated for San Bartolomé Loxicha [zam] by Beam de Azcona 2016/2022. No stress statement specifically for San Agustín Loxicha was found (Beam de Azcona 2008 gives only tentative tones for SAL; Salminen 2014 not accessible).

tone_statements.citation: Hernández Luna, Mario, Juliana de la Mora Gutiérrez & Juan Reyes Ruiz. 2026. La morfosintaxis y la prosodia del reporte directo en miahuateco. Semas (Universidad Autónoma de Querétaro) 7(14): 6-33. DOI 10.61820/s.2683-3301.v7n14.213.
tone_statements.quote: El miahuateco cuenta con cuatro tonos (A, B, BA, AB). En el Cuadro 1, mostramos un conjunto de contrastes tonales en la lengua. Además de estos, se presenta un rasgo. Cuadro 1. Contrastes tonales en miahuateco (Hernández y Herrera, 2024). A B AB BA le2 ‘diente’ le1 ‘nombre’ lo21 ‘cara’ le12 ‘caliente’ … En este sentido, el miahuateco cuenta con dos tonos de nivel A, B; dos de contorno AB, BA y un levantamiento del registro causado por un rasgo [+upper] que introduce el reporte directo
tone_statements.translation: Miahuatec has four tones (A, B, BA, AB). In Table 1 we show a set of tonal contrasts in the language. Besides these, a feature is present. Table 1. Tonal contrasts in Miahuatec (Hernández & Herrera 2024). A B AB BA le2 'tooth' le1 'name' lo21 'face' le12 'hot' … In this sense, Miahuatec has two level tones A, B; two contour tones AB, BA, and a raising of the register caused by a [+upper] feature that introduces the direct report
tone_statements.locator: p. 9, 'Breves generalidades fonológicas' with Cuadro 1 + p. 28, end of 'Algunas propiedades entonativas del discurso directo en miahuateco'
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Four tones: two level (A = high, B = low) and two contours (BA rising, AB falling), inventory taken from Hernández & Herrera 2024; F0 tracks show a register raise [+upper] over direct-speech reports.

tone_statements.citation: Hernández Luna, Mario Ulises & Juan Reyes Ruiz. 2024. Una mirada a la fonología segmental del Dìz’tè [dí'ztè] a través de un texto oral. Káñina, Revista de Artes y Letras (Universidad de Costa Rica) 48(1): 21-50 [Crossref: 1-29]. DOI 10.15517/rk.v48i1.58475
tone_statements.quote: El di'ztè distingue morfemas con cuatro melodías tonales: A, B, AB y BA. En la Tabla 4 que presentamos abajo, mostramos un conjunto de palabras con las cuatro melodías tonales básicas en palabras morfológicamente simples. [...] La implementación de los tonos se ve afectada en esta lengua por dos factores. En primer lugar, por el rasgo glotis constreñida y, en segundo lugar, por la consonante en coda de sílabas cerradas. [...] Este último hecho sugiere, además, que la unidad portadora del tono es la rima y no la mora como se ha sugerido en trabajos anteriores (Hernández, 2019).
tone_statements.translation: Di'ztè distinguishes morphemes with four tonal melodies: H, L, HL and LH. In Table 4 below we show a set of words with the four basic tonal melodies in morphologically simple words. [...] The implementation of the tones is affected in this language by two factors: first, the feature [constricted glottis] and, second, the coda consonant of closed syllables. [...] This last fact further suggests that the tone-bearing unit is the rhyme and not the mora, as suggested in earlier work (Hernández 2019).
tone_statements.locator: section 'Tonos' following 'Contrastes por fonación'; Tabla 4 'Melodías tonales en palabras morfológicamente simples en dí'ztè'

tone_statements.citation: Hernández Luna, Mario Ulises. 2021 [Crossref issued 2020-12-20]. Acento y legitimación del rasgo [glotis constreñida] en miahuateco. Lingüística Mexicana. Nueva Época 3(1): 151-171 (Dossier). DOI 10.62190/amla.lmne.2021.3.1.6 (the DOI printed on the OJS page, 10.62190/amla.lmne.2021.3.1.409, is not registered)
tone_statements.quote: En esta lengua hay cuatro tonos, alto (A), bajo (B), descendente (AB) y ascendente (BA). La manifestación fonética de estos cuatro tonos depende de dos factores: el rasgo [GC] y el tipo de consonante en coda (Hernández 2019). [...] Los tonos alto y ascendente promueven la realización del rasgo [GC] en términos del grado de la tensión laríngea como un corte glotal, mientras que el tono bajo favorece la realización del rasgo [GC] como voz laringizada.
tone_statements.translation: In this language there are four tones, high (H), low (L), falling (HL) and rising (LH). The phonetic manifestation of these four tones depends on two factors: the feature [CG] and the type of coda consonant (Hernández 2019). [...] High and rising tones favour realisation of [CG], in terms of degree of laryngeal tension, as a glottal stop, while low tone favours realisation of [CG] as laryngealised voice.
tone_statements.locator: HTML galley, passage following Tabla 2 'Inventario consonántico del miahuateco' and Tabla 3 'Sistema vocálico del miahuateco'; print pp. 151-171

tone_statements.citation: Hernández Luna, Mario Ulises. 2021. Fonología del miahuateco: sincronía, diacronía y clasificación. Tesis de doctorado, El Colegio de México.
tone_statements.quote: El zapoteco de Santo Domingo de Morelos cuenta con cinco melodı́as tonales superficiales que se reducen a cuatro tonos fonológicos en el nivel subyacente. … En sı́ntesis, propongo que el sistema tonal del zapoteco de Santo Domingo de Morelos se compone de 4 tonos, dos de nivel y dos de contorno y que voy a transcribir como /A/, /B/, /BA/ y /AB/. … El sistema tonal es el más promiente de las tres lenguas con cuatro tonos fonológicos; dos de nivel: /A/ y /B/ y dos de contorno /BA/ y /AB/.
tone_statements.translation: Santo Domingo de Morelos Zapotec has five surface tonal melodies which reduce to four phonological tones at the underlying level. … In sum, I propose that the tonal system of Santo Domingo de Morelos Zapotec consists of 4 tones, two level and two contour, which I will transcribe as /A/, /B/, /BA/ and /AB/. … The tonal system is the most prominent of the three languages, with four phonological tones; two level: /A/ and /B/, and two contour /BA/ and /AB/.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 228-232, ch. 4 s.4.3.2 "El tono" ((4.38) Patrones tonales p. 229; Cuadro 4.7 p. 230; synthesis p. 231; Sintesis p. 232)
tone_statements.summary: Four phonological tones: two level (high /A/, low /B/) and two contours (rising /BA/, falling /AB/), from five surface melodies; low downstepped after low; separate iambic (weak-strong) word stress.

La manifestación fonética de estos cuatro tonos depende de dos factores: el rasgo [GC] y el tipo de consonante en coda (Hernández 2019). [...] Los tonos alto y ascendente promueven la realización del rasgo [GC] en términos del grado de la tensión laríngea como un corte glotal, mientras que el tono bajo favorece la realización del rasgo [GC] como voz laringizada.
sources.locator: HTML galley, passage following Tabla 2 'Inventario consonántico del miahuateco' and Tabla 3 'Sistema vocálico del miahuateco'; print pp. 151-171
sources.note: States Miahuatec has four tones, high (A), low (B), falling (AB), rising (BA), whose phonetic realisation depends on [GC] and coda consonant type; high and rising tones favour realisation of [GC] as a glottal stop, low tone as creaky voice; contrasts Coatec (glottal 'tone', tonal contrasts neutralised under glottalisation) with Miahuatec and San Bartolo Yautepec, which keep tonal contrasts in non-modal voice; main topic is stress (metrical structure) as the licenser of [GC].

tone.translation: In this language there are four tones, high (H), low (L), falling (HL) and rising (LH). The phonetic manifestation of these four tones depends on two factors: the feature [CG] and the type of coda consonant (Hernández 2019). [...] High and rising tones favour realisation of [CG], in terms of degree of laryngeal tension, as a glottal stop, while low tone favours realisation of [CG] as laryngealised voice.

tone.quote: Figure 2 shows the tonal correspondences found between the San Baltazar Loxicha (SBalL) and Coatlán dialects of Coatec and the San Agustín Mixtepec (SAM), San Agustín Loxicha (SAL), and San Bartolomé Loxicha (SBarL) dialects of Miahuatec. … Focusing on A-J, I have reconstructed high, low, and rising tones, occurring with and without the conditioning environment of glottalization. … Falling tones in the varieties considered seem to have developed recently from high tone (Coatec) and low tone (SBarL) and there are no mid tones in the varieties examined.

tone.quote: El zapoteco de Santo Domingo de Morelos cuenta con cinco melodı́as tonales superficiales que se reducen a cuatro tonos fonológicos en el nivel subyacente. … En sı́ntesis, propongo que el sistema tonal del zapoteco de Santo Domingo de Morelos se compone de 4 tonos, dos de nivel y dos de contorno y que voy a transcribir como /A/, /B/, /BA/ y /AB/. … El sistema tonal es el más promiente de las tres lenguas con cuatro tonos fonológicos; dos de nivel: /A/ y /B/ y dos de contorno /BA/ y /AB/.
tone.locator: pp. 228-232, ch. 4 s.4.3.2 "El tono" ((4.38) Patrones tonales p. 229; Cuadro 4.7 p. 230; synthesis p. 231; Sintesis p. 232)
tone.translation: Santo Domingo de Morelos Zapotec has five surface tonal melodies which reduce to four phonological tones at the underlying level. … In sum, I propose that the tonal system of Santo Domingo de Morelos Zapotec consists of 4 tones, two level and two contour, which I will transcribe as /A/, /B/, /BA/ and /AB/. … The tonal system is the most prominent of the three languages, with four phonological tones; two level: /A/ and /B/, and two contour /BA/ and /AB/.
tone.summary: Four phonological tones: two level (high /A/, low /B/) and two contours (rising /BA/, falling /AB/), from five surface melodies; low downstepped after low; separate iambic (weak-strong) word stress.
tone.says: Four phonological tones: two level (high /A/, low /B/) and two contours (rising /BA/, falling /AB/), from five surface melodies; low downstepped after low; separate iambic (weak-strong) word stress.
